LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 5.1.3 AUDIENCE AWARENESS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.1: Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 5.1.3 Audience awareness
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 5.1.3 Audience awareness, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How should I speak to someone who is near? 2. How should I sign to someone who is near?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 5.1.3 Audience awareness together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration:signing skills as learner signs clearly for observer (s) to get the communication well.

• Learning to learn:development of relationships as learner works in pairs to present songs and poems in class and during parade

and get feedback on clarity, audibility and fluency.

Values:
• Respect: Patience as learners works together in the listening and projection of voices in the classroom.

• Peace: Love as learners work together in harmony as some talk and others listen so as to give feedback as a way of peer

assessment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Socio-economic awareness as the learner learns that in the neighbourhood there are businesses and organizations that help in

money making.

Link to other Learning Area:

creative activities (music) as learners present songs during parade and get feedback on clarity to audience.

Suggested Learning Resources:

assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as hearing aids and amplifiers, signed audio visual recordings, relevant

digital devices, online resources,
